pubcol-w-0fcac35afc041c97.definition_en: to have a polite, casual conversation about unimportant things
collocations: make small talk with a colleague
make small talk at a party
pubcol-w-0fcac35afc041c97.example_simple: We made small talk about the weather while we waited for the bus.
pubcol-w-0fcac35afc041c97.example_complex: Although he found it awkward, he forced himself to make small talk with the other guests before the meeting began.

pubcol-w-0de192c342517ae1.definition_en: to prepare tea by adding hot water to tea leaves or a tea bag
pubcol-w-0de192c342517ae1.example_simple: I'll make some tea while you sit down and relax.
pubcol-w-0de192c342517ae1.example_complex: She always makes a fresh pot of tea for her guests the moment they arrive.

pubcol-w-8440b5a36be7f445.definition_en: to organise the details of a journey, such as transport and accommodation
collocations: make travel arrangements for the team
pubcol-w-8440b5a36be7f445.example_simple: My assistant will make the travel arrangements for the conference.
pubcol-w-8440b5a36be7f445.example_complex: Before the delegation could leave, someone had to make travel arrangements for flights, hotels and local transfers.

pubcol-w-662797b75bbffe71.definition_en: to compensate for something bad or missing
collocations: try to make up for it
pubcol-w-662797b75bbffe71.example_simple: He bought her flowers to make up for forgetting her birthday.
pubcol-w-662797b75bbffe71.example_complex: The team worked overtime for weeks to make up for the delays caused earlier in the project.

pubcol-w-cc87206d63b7ef40.definition_en: to reach a decision after considering something
pubcol-w-cc87206d63b7ef40.example_simple: Hurry up and make up your mind — the shop is closing soon.
pubcol-w-cc87206d63b7ef40.example_complex: After weeks of hesitation, she finally made up her mind to accept the job abroad.

pubcol-w-f6155390d02d3d6e.definition_en: to use something for a useful purpose; take advantage of
pubcol-w-f6155390d02d3d6e.example_simple: You should make use of the library while you are a student.
pubcol-w-f6155390d02d3d6e.example_complex: The company made effective use of social media to reach a much wider audience.

pubcol-w-1d98bd7d93c4152e.example_simple: As a boy he loved to make verses about the sea.
pubcol-w-1d98bd7d93c4152e.example_complex: In his spare time the professor made verses that he never dared to show anyone.

pubcol-w-9f5dd36b60107ebb.definition_en: to produce or supply something quickly (informal)
pubcol-w-9f5dd36b60107ebb.example_simple: Come on, make with the popcorn — the film is starting!
pubcol-w-9f5dd36b60107ebb.example_complex: The audience grew restless, waiting for the comedian to make with the punchlines they had paid for.

pubcol-w-52f00462a3e4063b.definition_en: to earn money through work or business
pubcol-w-52f00462a3e4063b.example_simple: She makes money by selling handmade jewellery.
pubcol-w-52f00462a3e4063b.example_complex: Many young entrepreneurs are finding new ways to make money without ever setting up a physical shop.

pubcol-w-2949450545931999.definition_en: to cause a fierce quarrel or angry commotion
pubcol-w-2949450545931999.example_simple: Her comment about the budget really made the fur fly at the meeting.
pubcol-w-2949450545931999.example_complex: Announcing the redundancies without warning was bound to set the fur flying among the staff.

pubcol-w-794e54272ac24266.definition_en: to firmly ask for something or place a heavy requirement on someone
collocations: make a demand for higher pay
pubcol-w-794e54272ac24266.example_simple: The job makes a lot of demands on my time.
pubcol-w-794e54272ac24266.example_complex: The union made a formal demand for better working conditions before agreeing to end the strike.

pubcol-w-010fd9d734bb575d.definition_en: to earn more money than you spend in a business activity
collocations: make a profit on the sale
pubcol-w-010fd9d734bb575d.example_simple: The shop finally made a profit in its second year.
pubcol-w-010fd9d734bb575d.example_complex: By cutting costs and raising prices slightly, the company managed to make a modest profit despite the recession.

pubcol-w-07a888bfe45fd670.definition_en: to silently express a hope for something to come true
collocations: make a wish and blow out the candles
close your eyes and make a wish
pubcol-w-07a888bfe45fd670.example_simple: Make a wish before you blow out the candles!
pubcol-w-07a888bfe45fd670.example_complex: As the shooting star crossed the sky, she closed her eyes and made a wish she had held for years.

pubcol-w-4c5fdae83be76f97.definition_en: to complain or become excited about something unimportant
pubcol-w-4c5fdae83be76f97.example_simple: Don't make a fuss — it's only a small scratch.
pubcol-w-4c5fdae83be76f97.example_complex: He made such a fuss over the tiny error that everyone forgot how well the rest of the report was written.

pubcol-w-167162de4b3ff8f8.definition_en: to make a place dirty or untidy, or to spoil something
collocations: make a mess in the kitchen
make a real mess of it
pubcol-w-167162de4b3ff8f8.example_simple: The children made a mess in the living room.
pubcol-w-167162de4b3ff8f8.example_complex: By trying to fix the software himself, he only made a bigger mess of the whole system.

pubcol-w-19cb20500be67d49.definition_en: to ask for information about something
collocations: make an inquiry about a booking
pubcol-w-19cb20500be67d49.example_simple: I made an inquiry about the price of the tickets.
pubcol-w-19cb20500be67d49.example_complex: The journalist made discreet inquiries into the company's finances before publishing her story.

pubcol-w-35a7dc833a8032c4.definition_en: to produce sound, especially loud or unwanted sound
pubcol-w-35a7dc833a8032c4.example_simple: Please don't make so much noise — the baby is sleeping.
pubcol-w-35a7dc833a8032c4.example_complex: The old engine made a worrying noise every time the car climbed a steep hill.

pubcol-w-b24712037738d33f.ipa: /ˌmeɪkɪŋ ə ˈmaʊntɪn aʊt əv ə ˈmoʊlhɪl/
pubcol-w-b24712037738d33f.definition_en: to treat a small problem as if it were far more serious than it is
collocations: stop making a mountain out of a molehill
always making a mountain out of a molehill
it's just making a mountain out of a molehill
pubcol-w-b24712037738d33f.example_simple: It's only a small delay — you're making a mountain out of a molehill.
pubcol-w-b24712037738d33f.example_complex: Rather than making a mountain out of a molehill, the manager calmly explained that the minor bug would be fixed within the hour.

pubcol-w-08a7c28510a26c3b.definition_en: a catastrophe caused by human activity rather than nature
collocations: a man-made disaster on a huge scale
pubcol-w-08a7c28510a26c3b.example_simple: The oil spill was a man-made disaster that harmed thousands of animals.
pubcol-w-08a7c28510a26c3b.example_complex: Unlike earthquakes or floods, many man-made disasters could be avoided with stricter safety regulations.
pubcol-w-08a7c28510a26c3b.vi_meaning_correction: thảm họa do con người gây ra (khác với thiên tai như động đất, lũ lụt, bão)

pubcol-w-dfe0ef17be118ac0.example_simple: The lion shook its thick mane in the sun.
pubcol-w-dfe0ef17be118ac0.example_complex: Her long mane of golden hair fell loose over her shoulders as she turned to face the crowd.
